defects_found.description: Hebrew fragments are frequently quoted with niqqud (vowel points) intact but without cantillation/trope marks (and occasional meteg), relative to SP/2Sam_oshb.txt's full Masoretic pointing. In every instance checked, consonants and vowel points match the source verse exactly once cantillation is set aside; a smaller set of fragments are bare consonantal glosses (no points at all) used as light interlinear translation aids rather than diplomatic quotations. No case of wrong consonants, wrong vowels, or wrong verse was found.

The fragment '[קרי הַכְּרֵתִיָ]' at 20:23 adds the qere label 'קרי' as editorial annotation; SP/2Sam_oshb.txt itself just juxtaposes the ketiv (הכרי) and qere (הַכְּרֵתִי) forms without markup. The underlying ketiv/qere identification is verified accurate against the real Masoretic phenomenon at this verse and is not collapsed or confused; only the added label is not literally present in the source file.

Both rows quote מְפיבֹשֶת (Mephibosheth) as one word, consistent with every other occurrence of the name in SP/2Sam_oshb.txt (4:4, 9:6/10/11/12/13, 19:26, 19:31). Only SP/2Sam_oshb.txt's own text at 21:7 renders the name with an anomalous internal space (מְפי בֹשֶת), which looks like a source-file tokenization quirk rather than a row error; content and meaning are unaffected.
